_comment: S3 nucleation / sink-density study.  Same single condition as S2 (330 C,
G = 1e-6) so S3 rows are directly comparable to the S2 and LOOP_COAL
baselines run on the identical theta (S2 row 3100, F_hi_open conversion:
Motivation (2026-08-16): the LOOP_COAL prototype showed the <111> size
deficit is NOT a missing coarsening channel -- 300x the coarsening rate
buys only +10% in d_111 before saturating.  The inventory check says the
model already holds the RIGHT total SIA content in <111> loops
(7.66e24 /m3 at 0.02 dpa vs ~6.3e24 for an experiment-like N and d); it
partitions that inventory over ~20x too many loops that are ~17x too
small.  So the lever is nucleation density, not coarsening.
Target at 0.02 dpa: N_111 = 1.1e22 m^-3 with d_111 = 6.5 nm -- the pair
that is simultaneously satisfiable at the model's CURRENT inventory.

S330.label: 330 C, G=1e-6 (proxy for BOR-60 330 C / 15 dpa)

admissibility_rule.note: delta_FP is blind to SIA-axis truncation (the <100> pile-up held delta_FP at 1e-8 while 96% of content sat at n=I), so grid adequacy is judged by pile/occupancy. It is NOT blind to the VACANCY axis -- delta_FP rests on the swelling identity S = S_I + Delta J^d and S is the vacancy inventory. The vacancy axis was unchecked until 2026-08-02; at the check_machine probe (V=120) mean_n_v moved 18.7->136 and swelling 58x on going to V=240.
